body:
Follow-up with an end-to-end A/B that separates async and sync scheduling, since my first GPU run did not.

**Setup.** RTX 3080 Ti, Qwen3-0.6B, main `a2fb482732` vs. main + this change. `prefix_repetition` with a 16384-token shared prefix, 128 suffix, 256 output (`--temperature 0 --ignore-eos`), 200 prompts, concurrency 32. `--num-gpu-blocks-override 1130` leaves room for about 4 running requests, so the rest wait at the head with a 16k-token prefix-cache hit. 3 rounds, with base and fix interleaved; every run has its commit and the md5 of `kv_cache_manager.py` logged.

| median of 3 rounds | main | this change | per-round paired diff |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--no-async-scheduling`, output tok/s | 258.50 | 282.56 (**+9.3%**) | +22.8 / +26.9 / +23.6 |
| `--no-async-scheduling`, median ITL | 20.44 ms | 18.48 ms (−9.6%) | −1.96 / −2.02 / −1.92 |
| async (default), output tok/s | 335.45 | 338.40 (+0.9%) | +0.2 / +4.7 / +1.0 |
| async (default), median ITL | 15.27 ms | 15.29 ms | — |

All 2400 requests completed with no failures. Generated texts match between the two builds about as often as they match between two runs of main (184–199/200 vs. 185/200), so I see no output change attributable to the patch.

**Reading.** The saving is real when the scheduler runs on the critical path: about 9% throughput under sync scheduling, with all three paired differences on the same side. Under the default async scheduling the scheduler overlaps the GPU step, and the difference is inside run-to-run noise in this setup. My first run (1.7B, 8k prefix) was most likely async as well, which would explain why it showed nothing.

By `VllmConfig`'s defaults, sync scheduling is what pooling models get, and so do speculative-decoding methods outside EAGLE/MTP/draft-model/NGram-GPU/DSpark/DFlash, executors without async support, and PP>1 on the V1 model runner. So the question from my first comment becomes more concrete: is a ~9% gain for those configurations, with no measurable change under the default async path, enough to justify +126/−5 lines in `kv_cache_manager.py`? If so I'm happy to open the PR. If not, I'll leave it here.

(AI-assisted investigation; I reviewed the code and ran the benchmarks myself. Raw results and the analysis script are available on request.)

Same A/B rerun on a second GPU (RTX 4090, Xeon Gold 6430). The script, parameters and both builds are identical to the run above: the md5 of `kv_cache_manager.py` matches on both builds. 3 rounds, base and fix interleaved, 12/12 runs with 200/200 completed.

| median of 3 rounds | main | this change | per-round paired diff |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--no-async-scheduling`, output tok/s | 409.89 | 457.52 (**+11.6%**) | +41.2 / +50.9 / +48.2 |
| `--no-async-scheduling`, median ITL | 14.04 ms | 12.19 ms (−13.2%) | −1.72 / −1.95 / −1.85 |
| `--no-async-scheduling`, median TTFT | 14971 ms | 13406 ms (−10.5%) | — |
| async (default), output tok/s | 580.86 | 583.66 (+0.5%) | +1.2 / +3.4 / +2.9 |
| async (default), median ITL | 9.62 ms | 9.64 ms | — |
| async (default), p99 ITL | 45.47 ms | 47.28 ms (+4.0%) | +1.4 / +2.2 / +1.1 |

The sync result reproduces on a second machine and is somewhat larger here, which fits the scheduler being a larger share of a shorter GPU step. Under default async scheduling the change is again within a few percent either way: throughput is slightly higher in all three rounds, and p99 ITL is slightly worse in all three. With only three rounds I wouldn't read either as a real effect. I haven't looked into the p99 ITL difference.

Generated texts match between builds about as often as between two runs of the same build (171–184/200 vs. 172–180/200).

So the picture is unchanged: a clear gain for configurations that run the scheduler synchronously, and nothing measurable on the default async path.
